title: Audit logs & admin activity review - Halo Security
summary: Redwood and Halo Security reviewed audit logging and admin activity capabilities: what events are recorded, retention defaults and options, export/integration pathways (S3/GCS, syslog, Kafka, SIEM), encryption and CMEK/HSM options for Private, RBAC/SSO/SCIM basics, and SOC2/ISO alignment. Agreed to provide an export sample and security pack; Halo requested a 12-month retention option and an immutability/tamper-evidence whitepaper.
topics: What audit events are captured (admin console, API, keys, token usage)
Log schema and fields (actor, action, resource, request id, IP, user-agent)
Retention defaults vs custom retention (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
Export options: S3/GCS, syslog, Kafka, webhook, BigQuery, Splunk/Datadog connectors
Encryption: at-rest SSE, customer-managed keys (CMEK), HSM for Private
Compliance posture: SOC 2 / ISO 27001 controls around logs
action_items: Mark to send sample audit log export (JSON) and field-level legend by 2026-12-03
Lena to share SOC 2 and ISO 27001 certs and the audit-logs whitepaper by 2026-12-04
Halo to confirm required retention policy (90d vs 365d) and target SIEM by 2026-12-07
next_steps: Schedule a follow-up demo focused on SIEM integration (week of 12/7)
Halo to provide their SIEM ingestion details and retention requirement
transcript:
[00:00:00] Lena Ortiz: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Today we're going to run through Redwood's audit logs and admin activity, capture what Halo needs for compliance and SIEM ingestion. Quick intros?
[00:00:12] Priya Rao: Hi, Priya Rao, CISO at Halo. We're primarily concerned about tamper-evidence, export to our Splunk, and 12-month retention for audit trails.
[00:00:23] Mark Chen: Great, Priya. I’m Mark, SE on the security row, I'll handle the technical bits. Quick note on naming: sometimes the auto-transcripts show K-M-S instead of KMS, so apologies up front.
[00:00:35] David Kim: David here, DevOps. We need to know what exact fields we get per event--like IP, user agent, request payloads, model id, request_id, and whether API key usage shows the key id only or whole key.
[00:00:47] Mark Chen: Good question. At a high level, logs capture: timestamp, actor (user id or service principal), action (api.create, console.login, model.invoke, key.create, key.revoke), resource id, request_id, org_id, client_ip, user_agent, response_code, and truncated request/response metadata. API keys are logged by key-id only, keys themselves never appear.
[00:01:05] Ana Torres: When you say truncated metadata, does that include prompt text? We have PII concerns and want prompts redacted unless we opt in.
[00:01:14] Mark Chen: By default, we do not log full prompt text in audit logs; we log metadata about the call and whether content was accessed. For customers who enable debug exports in Dedicated or Private, you can opt-in to more verbose logs, but we'd recommend redaction rules and token masking.
[00:01:29] Samir Patel: How about admin console actions? We need to see who changed RBAC roles, SSO configs, SCIM provisioning events.
[00:01:36] Mark Chen: Admin console events are captured: role changes, user invites, role grants, SSO/SAML config changes, SCIM sync status. Each event includes before/after values where applicable and a diff summary.
[00:01:49] Priya Rao: Are those diffs stored forever, or are they subject to retention?
[00:01:53] Mark Chen: They're subject to the same retention policy. Hosted default is 90 days of high-fidelity logs; we also keep metered indices longer for aggregated metrics. Dedicated customers can request custom retention windows and we support 365 days plus archive exports for regulatory needs. Private deployments are fully customer-controlled.
[00:02:07] Lena Ortiz: To add, we can provide immutable exports into your S3/GCS bucket for long-term retention and WORM policies, which satisfies many audit requirements.
[00:02:16] David Kim: Good. What's the export format and how do we stream to Splunk?
[00:02:20] Mark Chen: Exports can be ad-hoc JSON dumps, periodic batch exports to S3/GCS, or streaming via Kafka/syslog/webhook. For Splunk we typically recommend syslog or S3 ingestion with our export schema; we have connectors and a docs page with example Kinesis/Splunk config. We also support BigQuery and Pub/Sub for GCP customers.
[00:02:38] Ana Torres: Is there a native connector for Datadog or Elastic?
[00:02:41] Mark Chen: We have example recipes for Datadog and Elastic. For Dedicated we can enable a near-real-time push to your ES cluster via Kafka. For Hosted customers, we push batched files to your S3 bucket which your SIEM ingests.
[00:02:54] Priya Rao: Encryption: do logs at rest use customer-managed keys? We have a requirement to control encryption keys.
[00:03:00] Mark Chen: Yes, we support CMEK for Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports server-side encryption with Redwood-managed keys by default, and we can enable customer-managed KMS for enterprise agreements. Private includes HSM support and FIPS-compliant modules if you need hardware-backed keys.
[00:03:15] Samir Patel: And for transit? TLS? Mutual TLS?
[00:03:18] Mark Chen: All exports are TLS 1.2+; for streaming to customer endpoints we can do mTLS for dedicated/private.
[00:03:24] David Kim: Are logs tamper-evident? We need immutability guarantees for investigation chains.
[00:03:29] Mark Chen: We provide immutability options: write-once exports to S3 with WORM, and for Dedicated we can enable signed append-only logs with cryptographic hashes and key rotation policies. For Private you control the ledger. We'll pull together a whitepaper describing the tamper-evidence mechanism.
[00:03:45] Lena Ortiz: Also, our audit trails include API and console activity plus service-level events: model rollout changes, quantization/patch updates, configuration rollbacks, and routing policy changes.
[00:03:55] Ana Torres: Does the log include which model variant was invoked and latency metrics?
[00:03:58] Mark Chen: Yes, model id, model version, latency, token counts, cost metric, and the node id that served the request (for Dedicated). Some of those fields are only present in detailed exports, not the default concise audit view.
[00:04:11] Priya Rao: From a compliance POV, SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 controls are relevant. Do your logs support linking evidence to controls?
[00:04:19] Lena Ortiz: Our SOC 2 and ISO reports are in the security pack we'll send. The logs are structured so you can map events to control objectives (e.g., access controls, change management). We'll provide mapping notes.
[00:04:30] David Kim: How about SCIM provisioning events? We'll need delta events when user attributes change for automated reconciliation.
[00:04:36] Mark Chen: SCIM events include full events for create/update/delete plus attribute diffs. We also emit heartbeat/last-sync events so you can monitor the sync health.
[00:04:47] Priya Rao: Any rate limits on log exports? We have a high-volume plan; we need near-real-time forensics during incidents.
[00:04:54] Mark Chen: For Hosted the default export rate is batched; near-real-time streaming is available on Dedicated and Private. For high-volume Hosted customers we can arrange a dedicated streaming pipeline as part of an enterprise agreement.
[00:05:05] Samir Patel: On the legal side, how long do you store admin audit logs for older accounts? Suppose a user is terminated, can we still see their prior actions?
[00:05:13] Mark Chen: Yes, all historical events within the retention window remain: deleting a user does not remove the historical audit entries. We treat audit logs as immutable for the retention period.
[00:05:23] Priya Rao: If we need 12 months retention of high-fidelity logs, what's the cost/approach?
[00:05:28] Lena Ortiz: For Dedicated it's a configuration option; pricing is usage+storage. For Hosted we offer a paid retention addon (12 months), and we can pipeline exports to your S3 with lifecycle policies to reduce cost. We'll include a rough estimate in the follow-up pricing note.
[00:05:41] David Kim: Do you capture cloud provider metadata (like GCP project id, AWS account, VPC id) when Private is deployed in our environment?
[00:05:48] Mark Chen: In Private and Dedicated deployments we can include host-level metadata, cloud provider identifiers, and pod/node metadata if you opt in to that telemetry. For Hosted we include org-level region info but not customer cloud metadata.
[00:05:59] Ana Torres: We use Splunk with a canonical schema. Can you include a mapping example?
[00:06:03] Mark Chen: Absolutely. We'll send a mapping JSON that aligns our fields to Splunk's common event format and an example ingestion pipeline.
[00:06:10] Priya Rao: A few follow-ups: 1) We want proof that keys never leave HSM in Private; 2) we want an immutable log whitepaper; 3) can you show a sample of a redacted export so our privacy team can validate?
[00:06:21] Lena Ortiz: Yes to all three. We'll include HSM notes, the whitepaper, and a redacted JSON export sample.
[00:06:28] David Kim: For SIEM mapping, can you include examples for both Splunk and BigQuery?
[00:06:33] Mark Chen: Yep. We'll add both.
[00:06:36] Samir Patel: Any blockers on retention for EU data residency? We need logs stored in EU for customers in EU.
[00:06:42] Mark Chen: We support region-based storage. Hosted customers can pick EU regions and we store logs in that region. Dedicated and Private obviously give full control. We'll note data residency options in the security pack.
[00:06:55] Priya Rao: Last thing, can you confirm that audit logs are covered in your SOC 2 report?
[00:06:59] Lena Ortiz: Yes, logging and monitoring controls are covered; we'll attach the relevant sections in the pack.
[00:07:04] Mark Chen: I'll follow up with a sample schema and a small demo of streaming to Splunk in the next call.
[00:07:10] Priya Rao: Sounds good. Thanks both.
[00:07:12] Lena Ortiz: Thanks everyone. Recap in the follow-up email with attachments and next meeting.
